key_insight: X-Reset turns human hand-object demonstrations into reset states, using them to solve exploration for object-centric RL without imitating the demonstrations themselves.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable training of generalist manipulation policies across different robots and object sets, with stronger zero-shot transfer potential for robotic systems.
method: Kinematically retarget hand-object demonstrations to noisy robot states rather than motion trajectories.
Filter out unstable retargeted states and sample the remaining ones as environment resets during RL.
Train with general-purpose object-centric rewards so the policy depends only on object state and goal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports generalist policies trained on 20 objects across three embodiments, with generalization to unseen objects, robustness to imperfect hand-pose estimates, and sim-to-real transfer.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of retargeted reset states and simulation stability filtering, so imperfect state estimation or mismatched dynamics could limit coverage.
paper_title: X-Reset: Scaling Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning via Cross-Embodiment Resets
